newsitem.title: USA: James Earl Ray's condition improves - hospital.
newsitem.headline: James Earl Ray's condition improves - hospital.

text.p: James Earl Ray, convicted assassin of civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., was reported to be improving Monday after another hospitalization for liver problems.

Ray's condition was upgraded from serious to fair, a spokeswoman at Columbia Nashville Memorial Hospital said. When moved from his prison cell Saturday night he was initially said to be in critical condition.
The hospital said it did not know when or whether Ray, 68, would be sent back to prison.
It was the third time in recent weeks that he has required hospital treatment. His family says he suffers from cirrhosis of the liver although he never drank and his liver and kidneys are failing.
Ray confessed to the 1968 slaying of King in Memphis, although he later recanted and claimed he was set up. He was sentenced to 99 years in prison.
